markers.notes: The interaction point tells you you got the Out-of-style Rouge Clothing, but doesn't actually give it.
Obtained when accepting help after being defeated in the Symbolic (any floor). Only good for that boss and must be obtained again for the next boss if wanted.

texts.text: ... I don't think we'll ever get to learn what's beyond these doors of the Fount.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: With endings both returned to my memory, I ruminate upon what the third might hold, and find myself becoming more curious... than afraid.

texts.speaker: Yi Sang
texts.text: It must have been a grueling struggle to bear it all without us. Now, let us stand together against yet another trial.
I took a moment to briefly vent about the things we'd gone through to Yi Sang.

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: Faust's judgment was, ultimately... correct.

texts.speaker: Faust
texts.text: Unlike... mine...
... I should probably leave her alone for now.

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Fie! To think that such a tale of adventure was almost forgotten whole...! Forsooth, there could be no greater horror...

texts.speaker: Don Quixote
texts.text: Simply say the word, and we shall sally forth once again toward the peak. I have faith in thee, Manager Esquire!
Don Quixote proclaims confidently with redoubled determination.

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: *puff*

texts.speaker: Ryōshū
texts.text: ... What was severed has been patched together again. Well, I think I appreciated it more than I'd have thought I would.
Araya rattles affirmatively.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: I see a bit of my old self in Meursault—burying his true feelings, hiding them from others... But there are differences, I think.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: What state must his heart be in, to continue moving despite the futility of it all?
Had a discussion about Meursault with Hong Lu.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: You alright, mate? I don't think you've ever had to rewind this much, even back inside that hellish meat train.

texts.speaker: Heathcliff
texts.text: I still remember how you used to squirm and thrash on the ground, screamin' about how much it hurt, and now you ain't even twitchin'. You're always all or nothin', eh?
Heathcliff tapped on my clock head for a while.

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... I get why you couldn't tell us about the loops, but hmm...

texts.speaker: Ishmael
texts.text: ... Okay, did you have to brush me off like that every single time, though? I know I ask a lot of questions, but it was like you just didn't want to deal with—
Got told off by Ishmael.

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Aside from feeling like I missed out due to the memory shenanigans... Hey, I wasn't half bad here, huh?

texts.speaker: Rodion
texts.text: Kinda wish I got to do more here than just one floor, but... hey, I was still pretty smooth~ huh?
Praised Rodya, who seemed pretty satisfied with herself.

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: So... I wonder what her deal was? She did help us at the end of the day, but...

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: ... I feel even more mystified than I was when I met Demian.
Sinclair still seems curious about the lady of the Fount.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: You've done excellent work so far, despite the demanding circumstances.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: I would expect no less from our Executive Manager.
Outis's over-the-top praise doesn't make me feel as uncomfortable as it used to at the start of our journey.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Boy, I'm sore all over... I'm all out of gas.

texts.speaker: Gregor
texts.text: Let's take it easy once we're out of here. You've gone through hell and back yourself, haven't you? You deserve the rest, Manager Bud.
Groused about corporate with Gregor.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: Now, we may ascend.
Meursault is as unflappable as ever.
The Sinners all look to me for judgment.
Red coat. Clock head on fire.
It's "me" in the mirror.
<color=#E1B643>Despite having faith in the idea that you can always choose, you've been unable to truly make a choice. So... escape. Escape from this fate, this system.</color>
A soft and warm peal of laughter brushes past the fingertips laid against the wall.
A pale light, reminiscent of the Golden Bough, glimmers beneath its surface.
A wall patched over with Golden Hide.
The presence is faint, but something about it feels like the Golden Bough.
... I've never sat on this chair before.
Then, is this even a "chair" from my point of view?
Questions like this have been cropping up ever since I entered this department store.
If I sit on this object, it will become a chair.
Without understanding why, I realize that I don't want to do that.
There is something scribbled on the signpost.
[Dante... Meursault... when you see this message, find me at Le Rouge Contemporary Hall. It's right up over here.]
[You didn't come this season either. Where... Where did... everyone go...?]
The scribbles continue all the way to the bottom of the signpost.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... Pwie seems to have left us messages.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <These notes look... ancient... The ones Pwie wrote at the top are so weathered that I can hardly read the words.>

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Everything was Liquidated. And Pwie kept searching for us after the end... until...>
There is something written in the corner.
[I cannot stay downstairs any longer. I must rise. I must devour. I must consume.]
A department store signpost that's been scribbled over with Pwie's messages. Just how many seasons have passed since the last message...?
A half-torn piece of leather is patched haphazardly over it.
[To think that the Voice would grace my humble Contemporary Hall in person...]
[Though we've been unable to find the group of strangers the Voice seeks...]
[... my label will finally be accepted into the Luxury Hall...]
Pwie must've gathered the Rouges here before heading to the Luxury Hall.
... Though I don't know how many seasons have passed since then. Could've been dozens, or even more.
According to this journal left behind by a Rouge, Pwie must've gathered the Rouges here before heading to the Luxury Hall.
... Though I don't know how many seasons have passed since then. Could've been dozens, or even more.

texts.speaker: Le Néant
texts.text: The basement... has fallen to bedlam. The great cycle yet persists, but it has now turned into a living hell where each devours the other.

texts.speaker: Le Néant
texts.text: Strangers. You must continue climbing if you seek to fulfill the Voice's will. The lower floors hold no purpose for you.

texts.speaker: Le Néant
texts.text: The strangers have done it. All is as she said.
There is an almost imperceptible vibration coming from the pipe. Upon leaning close to the opening, the vibration clears and turns into a voice.
[Dooo... As order... commandsssss...]
[Rememberrrrrr.... the paaaaaaaain...]
An ancient voice remains stuck in a cycle, pinned to the spot, and unable to leave.
Beneath the fallen podium is an Authenticity Certificate of Le Noir.
[Dear 3F Floor Manager.]
[In troubling times as these, where our Voice has fallen silent for reasons we are not at liberty to divulge, we of Le Noir desperately require your broadcast.]
[We implore you to visit Le Noir before even the very idea of trends becomes obsolete.]

texts.speaker: Sinclair
texts.text: ... Well, the podium is vacant. Maybe Le Noir has successfully recruited it?

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: Or the Rouges have. There's no evidence suggesting it's sided with either. Don't overlook the possibility that it was punished for refusing to choose a side.

texts.speaker: Outis
texts.text: But I believe it would have had to decide where its allegiance lay. There's no such thing as true neutrality to the end.
An Authenticity Certificate of Le Noir. There's another next to it, then another. They must've sent several.
A fallen pillar. It's only waist-high... Should be pretty easy to jump over.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Meursault, can't we just leap over this thing?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... I will make an attempt.
Meursault backed off a few feet from the pillar, stretched his arms and legs, then attempted a running jump...
... but immediately fell flat to the ground, as though something had tripped him mid-flight.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Sorry.>
Meursault dusted himself and got back to his feet, apparently unhurt.
A fallen waist-high pillar. Not even Meursault could jump over it.

markers.notes: Obtained when defeating 'The Sedimented' without accepting help.

texts.speaker: Le Néant
texts.text: Soon, we will all return to our homes—save for the Crimson God.

texts.speaker: Le Néant
texts.text: We owe everything to you, strangers.
The black couch—or what it looked like at first, at least—speaks to us.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: ... And here I was, surprised to see customers in the Furniture Hall again... I see that you are strangers.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: What happened to the other furnishings?

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: They all met a predictable end. Concerned solely about making themselves more expensive, they failed to consider who, in their right mind, would purchase them.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: They refused to lower their standards even after the Rouges have stripped them of anything even remotely valuable, and... well, the results lay plainly before you.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... So you're the last survivor?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: The Manager would like to know if you are the sole survivor.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: Oh yes, because I've chosen my buyer. And have had much to discuss with the sunshine, too.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: She has very high hopes for you, dear strangers.

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: "She"... as in the sunshine? Are you talking about Miss Carmen?

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: Hm... The sunshine is indeed a warm and kind being... but it does not lead, nor does it promise us a tomorrow.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: The sunshine is no different from any other natural phenomenon. The sunshine is as much a sunshine as rain is rain.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: The Voice of Le Néant, on the other hand... has promised me a tomorrow.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <... Le Néant.>

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: If you are weary, feel free to rest your feet awhile. Though I can't promise it'll be too comfortable.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <No thanks.>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: No thank you.

texts.speaker: Couch?
texts.text: Then farewell. I look forward to your deconstruction of this department store.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Renée...>

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: Ah... you've already made it this far.

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: It seems it won't be long before we can enjoy a little sunbathing.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Carmen—I mean, the sunshine... what exactly does it want?>

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: We wish to know... what the sunshine wants.

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: What a strange thing to ask. The sunshine... only wants what we want.

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: Even when the sunlight disagrees with us, so long as our wish, our emotion is sincere... it comes to want what we want.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <If that's the case, Meursault...>
Meursault had said that the sunshine was chatty. Irritatingly so.
Usually, those are the sort of words people use when something doesn't sit right with what they think...

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... What the sunshine whispered to me was entirely congruent to what I wanted, Manager.

texts.speaker: Dante
texts.text: <Then... what makes it so irritating?>
Meursault fell silent, sinking deeper into thought as if he could no longer bring himself to continue.
Almost as though something had frightened him.

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: Are you heading to 5F?

texts.speaker: Hong Lu
texts.text: Yes. We need to climb higher.

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: 5F... is where the Rouges have made themselves at home. That's where they are devouring the department store... bit by bit.

texts.speaker: Renée
texts.text: I do hope you'll make it past them... and find your way to the higher floors.

markers.notes: Obtained when defeating 'The Crimson God [Adulthood]' without accepting help.

texts.text:
You should be allowed to be who you are.
Not bound by anyone or anything.
There is a river that flows at the very bottom of the world.

As beings born as humans, we can't help but be affected by the dream of humanity that the river shares.
I won't deny that. It's just part of being human.
But "culture," which is acquired and unnatural, things that are determined by others... shouldn't define the shape.
I want you to be wholly yourself, even for a moment. In fact, I want mankind itself to be able to experience that.
I want to provide that opportunity, to grant the strength to achieve that.
After years upon years of toil and reflection, my junior's reached a certain enlightenment—and his philosophy was eventually set in a way that diverges from mine.
Ayin has the values I used to believe in and sought to convey to the world, and now seeks to give people... "tools." Clothes.
But my answer remains the same.

"You" must be allowed to remain wholly yourself.
Unshackled by anything.

markers.notes: Keep walking past Jeanne. Jeanne will trap you and shrink the room.

texts.speaker: Jeanne
texts.text: You've come this far, and now you're trying to run away?

texts.speaker: Jeanne
texts.text: It's futile, ma puce. You know this.

texts.speaker: Jeanne
texts.text: ... Is this your idea of a joke? Overwrought jokes are never that funny, you know. Why don't you quit messing around and take a seat?

markers.notes: Attack Jeanne. This prevents you from attacking again.

texts.speaker: Jeanne
texts.text: You're not even going to hesitate strike me? It's just my avatar, but... that makes me sad.

texts.speaker: Meursault
texts.text: ... I am sorry.

markers.notes: Meursault's House. Items may be difficult to find since the room is dark.

texts.text: I never miss a watering and regularly apply the Experience Fertilizer. But the leaves wither and fall anyway.
Empty Canned Experiences lie strewn about.
I feel a small sense of relief in that disorder. There is nothing quite like it in the experiences sealed inside those cans.
Even with the curtains drawn back, only faint rays of light shine through.
Still, I have to close them again before Mother comes out.
She does not want so much as a sliver of light getting in.
The coat I bought Mother with my first paycheck.
It was identical to what she always wore. Even so, my gift made her happy.
... No. That was merely my subjective perception. She only gave me a faint smile. She never said that it made her happy.
The chains that beheld the gaze.
